subject: Knowledge transfer workshop & post-session materials for ACME onboarding
messages:
From: Tim Perez <tim.perez@acme.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: anita.gomez@acme.com
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: knowledge transfer + hands-on workshop next week

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the kickoff call this morning. To keep momentum on our side, is it possible to run a 60–90 minute knowledge-transfer workshop next week that covers: setup checklist, typical API integration patterns, and a short troubleshooting walkthrough? We have two engineers (Anita and me) and a product manager who should attend.

Topology: we want to verify we can meet the latency SLOs described in the proposal and confirm token accounting for our prompt templates. Ideally a recording + slides afterward would be great.

Can you propose an agenda and a few time slots?

Best,
Tim
Head of Product, ACME Corp
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tim Perez <tim.perez@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: knowledge transfer + hands-on workshop next week

Hi Tim — great to hear from you and glad today's kickoff was useful. We can absolutely run a focused session. Proposed 75-minute plan:

1) 5m: introductions & goals
2) 15m: onboarding checklist (account, API keys, network/VPC notes, scopes)
3) 25m: live walkthrough — small integration example (Python + SDK) and demo of latency profiling in Console
4) 15m: troubleshooting common errors & interpretation of token breakdowns
5) 15m: Q&A + next steps (rollout checklist)

Attachments: redwood-kt-agenda-v1.pdf (agenda + pre-reqs).

Time slots we have open: Mon 2027-01-11 09:30–11:00 PT, Tue 2027-01-12 13:00–14:15 PT, Wed 2027-01-13 08:30–10:00 PT. We can record and deliver slides + a short action-item list after.

Marissa will share the pre-read and a short integration snippet; Evelyn will take notes and produce the recording.

Which slot works for your team?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Perez <tim.perez@acme.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: knowledge transfer + hands-on workshop next week

Hi Tim — adding a short prerequisites checklist here so the session can be hands-on:

- Confirm API key access and role permissions (instructions: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-kt-workshop)
- A sample repo or Postman collection (if you want us to run live requests against your prompts)
- Network: if you are using Private deployment, please confirm the VPC peering CIDR (if Hosted, no action needed)

Pre-reads attached: enablement-deck-acme-v1.pdf (includes console screenshots and example prompts).

If the 11th 09:30 PT slot works, we'll lock it and send a calendar invite with a short Google Meet link.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Tim Perez <tim.perez@acme.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Jan 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: knowledge transfer + hands-on workshop next week

Thanks — Mon 11th 09:30 PT works for us. We'll share a small sample repo before the session (Anita will upload by EOD Monday).

Two quick asks: can you include a short slide showing the cost implications of different batching settings, and can you confirm whether the latency profiling demo will include p99 and p95 numbers? Those are the metrics my infra lead will want to see.

Appreciate it — Tim
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Tim Perez <tim.perez@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Post-session plan & materials (recording link + action items)

Tim/Anita — thanks again for the session this morning. Summary + immediate artifacts below. Recording and slides attached: recording-20270109-ktw.mp4, enablement-deck-acme-v1.pdf.

Key outcomes:
- Verified API key provisioning and basic SDK integration with ACME sample repo.
- Ran a short latency profiling run: observed p50=42ms, p95=110ms, p99=210ms for the sample prompt shape; we discussed tuning batching to reduce cost while keeping p95 under 150ms.
- Action items captured and owners assigned.

Action items (owner / due):
- Anita: share expanded prompt set + additional edge-case examples (2027-01-13)
- Marissa: create a mutual action plan entry in HubSpot and attach the recording (2027-01-12)
- Soojin: prepare a recommended batching + quantization profile for ACME's workload and share (2027-01-14)

Links: recording (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-kt-workshop), workshop deck attached.

If anything in the notes is off, flag it and I will update. We'll check in on the MAP next week.

— Soojin
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tim Perez <tim.perez@acme.com>, Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@acme.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: MAP & next checkpoint

Folks — I created the mutual action plan in HubSpot and linked the recording and deck. Next checkpoint: Wed 2027-01-20 for a progress review on integration and cost tuning.

HubSpot MAP: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345

Thanks everyone — please reach out if timelines slip.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
